title: Rivian's Boss Spills the Beans: Buttons Rule, Cybertruck Flops, and a Secret Plan!
summary: Have you ever seen a car with no buttons and thought, "How do I even turn on the radio?" Rivian's boss, RJ Scaringe, loves buttons. He says they just feel right. But his company makes electric trucks and SUVs, and they're in a wild race. They've lost billions of dollars, but they also got a huge investment from Volkswagen and Uber. Now, all eyes are on their new R2 SUV. It's supposed to be the car for everyone — not too pricey, super cool. RJ admits if the R2 flops, they'd have to shrink the company big time. Why? Because they built giant parking lots, service centers, and even design their own computer chips, all expecting to sell tons of R2s. He also dished on other cars. The Tesla Cybertruck? "Very, very niche," he said. It's so wild-looking that it pushes people away. The Ferrari Luce? He thinks the inside is gorgeous, with amazing buttons and switches. And Polestar? Their cars look great but the price and features just haven't clicked with buyers. RJ's big dream is to give us more electric choices. Right now, two Teslas hog half the market. "That's not healthy," he says. "We need way more options!" So, will the R2 be the hero Rivian needs? Fingers crossed!
why_it_matters: The cars you might drive someday could have buttons or touchscreens, and having more electric choices means better designs and prices for everyone.

background_read: Rivian is an American electric vehicle company founded in 2009, best known for its R1T pickup truck and R1S SUV. RJ Scaringe (its founder and CEO) started the company with a dream of building adventure-ready electric vehicles.

Volkswagen, a giant German automaker, invested billions in Rivian, while Uber also put in money. Even so, Rivian has lost billions of dollars because building car factories and designing custom chips is very expensive.
The electric car market today is dominated by Tesla, but many experts and drivers want more brands to compete. That way, people can choose a car with the looks, features, and buttons they like.
Article_Structure: WHO: RJ Scaringe, the boss of electric truck and SUV maker Rivian.
WHAT: He shared his love for buttons, criticized the Cybertruck as too strange, and revealed that the future of his company depends on the R2 SUV's success.
WHERE: In a recent interview (no specific city mentioned).
WHY: Rivian spent a lot of money on factories and technology, and if the R2 flops, the company would have to shrink.

perspectives.description: They believe physical buttons are safer and more satisfying to use than touchscreens. They see the R2 as the car that will make electric adventure vehicles affordable and popular.
Some analysts worry Rivian's heavy spending and losses are too risky. If the R2 doesn't sell in huge numbers, the company might not survive, putting jobs and investors' money at risk.

Some people love the Cybertruck's futuristic look and think it's exactly what the market needs. They argue that Tesla's dominance proves it makes the best electric cars, and that 'niche' can still be highly successful.
